legal.terms.intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Wisecall. Please read them before you use the site. If you do not agree, please do not use it.

p: Wisecall is a marketplace. People who want advice (“seekers”) pay the mentor’s price to ask a question, or nothing if the mentor answers for free, and people with experience (“mentors”) answer it.
Mentors are independent people, not employees or agents of Wisecall. Wisecall is not a party to the advice itself. We provide the platform, take payment, and pay mentors.

You must be at least 16 years old to create an account and ask questions. If you are 16 or 17, you confirm when you sign up that your parent or guardian agrees to your using Wisecall. Mentors must be 18 or older and pass the ID check. Give us accurate information, including your real birth year and month, and keep your password private. You are responsible for everything that happens under your account.

If you are 16 or 17: you can ask mentors who answer for free. To ask a paid mentor, the person paying must be 18 or older (for example a parent) and agree to pay. Everything stays written, on Wisecall: contact details can’t be shared in either direction. For a time after launch, our team checks answers to people under 18 before they can be read. Mentors see only your first name and your question.
You must confirm your email address before you can apply to become a mentor. One person may have one account.

Answers on Wisecall are personal opinions and experience shared by individuals. They are not professional medical, legal, financial, tax, or psychological advice, and they do not create a doctor–patient, lawyer–client, or any other professional relationship, even when the mentor holds a licence in that field.

Do not use Wisecall for emergencies. If you or someone else may be in danger, contact your local emergency number. Always consult a qualified professional who can look at your full situation before you make important medical, legal, or financial decisions.

The price of a question is set by the mentor in Georgian lari (GEL) and shown before you pay. You pay when you send the question, by card on the secure payment page of our payment bank. Wisecall never sees or stores your full card details.
Your payment is held until the mentor answers. The mentor is paid only after they have answered.

Wisecall is not a bank. The payment is taken by a licensed Georgian bank that processes it for us. The amount you see is the amount you pay in lari, and any currency conversion by your own card issuer is outside our control.
If a mentor does not answer within 7 days of your payment, we refund you in full automatically. You do not need to ask.

After a question has been answered, payments are generally not refundable, because the answer has been delivered. We will refund in full when the answer is clearly spam, is empty or off-topic, or breaks these terms. To ask for this, contact us within 7 days of receiving the answer.
Disliking or disagreeing with an answer is not a reason for a refund. You can leave an honest review instead.
Refunds go back to the original payment method. Your bank may need several business days to show them. Please contact us before starting a chargeback, so we can fix the problem first.

If you apply to be a mentor, you promise that everything you tell us about yourself is true, including your job title, experience, qualifications, the story of your experience, and the evidence you provide. Pretending to be someone you are not, claiming credentials you do not have, or using someone else’s work as your evidence leads to removal and may lead to legal action.

Mentors must: answer honestly and in good faith; answer within the deadline; stay within their real area of expertise; not present an answer as a diagnosis, legal opinion, or financial recommendation for a specific person; keep what seekers tell them confidential; and follow the laws that apply to them, including any licensing rules in their profession. Mentors reply to the free follow-up question within 3 days.
Mentors must not ask seekers to pay outside Wisecall, must not share a seeker’s question publicly without permission, and must not send spam or promote unrelated services.

Mentors are responsible for their own taxes on the money they earn. To be paid, a mentor must give Wisecall their full name and a valid Georgian IBAN in Settings. Until then their profile stays hidden and they cannot receive questions.

We review mentor applications partly automatically, as the Privacy Policy explains. We may approve or reject an application and remove a mentor at any time, for example if they get poor reviews, break these terms, or we cannot verify them. Every rejection is made by a person on our team, who tells you why; you can change your application and apply again.

How mentor payouts work: for each answered question, the mentor earns the price minus the Wisecall platform fee. This becomes payable 7 days after the answer, which is the period in which a buyer can ask for a refund. Wisecall then pays it by bank transfer to the IBAN the mentor gave, in periodic manual transfers. If a buyer is refunded after the mentor has already been paid, the refunded amount is deducted from the mentor’s next payout.

Wisecall keeps a platform fee from each paid question (currently 20% of the price). The rest goes to the mentor. Our payment provider also charges its own processing fees, which are covered by the platform fee. The fee for a specific payment is stored with that payment and does not change afterwards.
Mentors may answer for free. No fee is charged on free questions.

Do not use Wisecall to break the law, harass or threaten anyone, share hateful or sexual content, impersonate others, send spam, try to get around the platform’s security or payments, or collect other users’ data.
Do not include other people’s private information in a question. Do not submit a question that asks the mentor to help you do something illegal or harmful.

You own what you write. By posting it on Wisecall you give us permission to store it, show it to the people it is meant for, and, for a mentor’s public profile and reviews, display it on the site. We may remove content that breaks these terms.
A review shows the reviewer’s name and photo when their profile is public; otherwise it is shown as coming from an anonymous asker.

After a paid question has been answered, the person who asked and the mentor can each rate the other once: 1 to 5 stars and a few tags. The person who asked can also write a review of the mentor. The mentor can add a private note for the Wisecall team, which the asker never sees.

Ratings stay hidden until both people have rated, or until 7 days after the answer became readable for the buyer, whichever comes first. Until then you can change your rating; after that you cannot. You can rate for up to 30 days after the answer.

A mentor’s average, number of ratings, tags and written reviews are public on their profile, with the reviewer’s name and photo (or “Anonymous asker” if the reviewer’s profile is private). Mentors can see an asker’s rating on the question.

Rate honestly and only from your own experience of that question. A rating or review must not contain insults, threats, hate, personal data (yours or anybody else’s), advertising, or claims you know to be untrue. Mentors may not ask for, pay for or trade ratings, and may not pressure people to change them.

Anyone who is logged in can report a review. Wisecall may hide a review that breaks these rules, and records who decided and why. We do not remove a review only because it is critical. Hidden reviews do not count towards averages.
A very low average, for a mentor or for an asker, is checked by our team. It can lead to a warning, a limit or, for a mentor, suspension under the section on suspending and closing accounts.

We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms or puts others at risk. You can stop using Wisecall at any time. If we close your account without a breach on your part, we will refund any question you paid for that was not answered.

We try to keep Wisecall available and accurate, but we provide it “as is”. We cannot promise that every answer is correct, useful, or suitable for you, and we are not responsible for decisions you make based on an answer.

legal.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
legal.privacy.intro: This explains what personal data Wisecall collects, why, and what your rights are. We keep it to what we need to run the service.

p: Wisecall is responsible (the “controller”) for the personal data described here. You can reach us through the contact page on this site.
Account data: your name, email address, and a password (stored only as a one-way hash, never in readable form), plus your language choice.

Profile data: your username, photo, headline, current work or study, city, languages, short bio, and optional LinkedIn and website links. You choose who can see them: everyone, or only people you have had a question with (the profile of a mentor who is listed on Wisecall is always public). Photos are resized and stripped of hidden data such as the place they were taken. Your email address, bank details and verification documents are never shown on a profile.

Sign in with Google: if you choose “Continue with Google”, Google tells us your name, your email address, whether Google has verified that address, your picture, and an identifier of your Google account. We do not receive your Google password, and we get no access to your Google data beyond these basics. You can disconnect Google in Settings once you have set a password.

Mentor data: if you apply to be a mentor, your job title, field (niche), specialty tags, years of experience, the story of how you learned your field, a sample answer, your price, and the evidence you add (links to your work, a Georgian company registration code, an uploaded diploma or certificate, and optionally a confirmed work email). Your title, field, bio and price become public once you are approved. Your story, sample answer, evidence and email are never public.
Questions and answers: the questions you send, the answers you receive, and reviews you write.

Payment data: your card details are entered on our payment bank’s secure page and processed by the bank. We receive only the payment status, amount and the bank’s reference numbers. We never see or store your full card number. Mentors give us their full name and IBAN so we can pay them; the IBAN is stored encrypted and is visible only to the mentor and to Wisecall administrators who make the payouts.
Technical data: your IP address and basic request information appear in server logs and are used to prevent abuse (for example, limiting repeated login attempts).

Ratings and reviews: the stars, tags and written reviews you give or receive, and (for mentors) any private note to our team. A mentor’s ratings and written reviews are public. An asker’s rating is shown only as a badge, after 3 ratings. Private notes are read only by the Wisecall team.

Waiting list: if you join the waiting list, your email address, the field you chose, your language and, if you typed one in the home page’s search, your question (up to 300 characters, with any email address or phone number in it removed). Our team sees the questions without the email addresses, to decide which mentors to invite. The link in our email removes you from the list.

Every mentor is checked before they appear on Wisecall. This section explains what that involves and applies only to people who apply to be mentors. An application has three steps: identity, experience, and a review.

ID and selfie check: we use an identity verification provider, Didit (didit.me), to check a government ID document and a live selfie. You send your ID photos and selfie directly to the provider. Wisecall does not receive or store them. We receive and keep only the provider’s verification ID, the result (approved, declined or in review), your verified full name, date of birth and country, and the time of the check. Your verified name and date of birth are stored encrypted. From the date of birth the application uses only one fact: whether you are 18 or older. The provider handles your data under its own privacy policy and its agreement with us.

Names: we compare the name on your ID with your profile name and, in regulated fields, the name on your license. If they do not match, you can correct your profile name or a member of our team looks at it; it is never an automatic rejection. The name of your payout account holder is compared too, but only before we pay you: a different name holds the payout until our team has checked it.

Experience and evidence: you describe your experience and add at least one piece of evidence of any kind (a portfolio, your website, a social media page, publications, your company, a diploma, a product you made, testimonials). You do not need an employer. In regulated fields (such as medicine, law and finance) we also ask for your license or registration number and who issued it, and where there is no public register we can check, a copy of your license, certificate or diploma. License numbers and uploaded documents are stored encrypted and are visible only to the Wisecall administrators who review applications.
Video interview: only if our team asks for one before deciding. We keep the time of the call, the result and our reviewers’ notes.

Records: every decision is written to an audit log with who made it, when and why. Your public profile shows only badges for the checks you passed (for example “ID verified” and “Experience reviewed”) and the date of the check. It never shows your ID, date of birth, license number, evidence or documents.

Ongoing checks: after approval we keep watching quality. Your first answers may be reviewed before they reach the buyer, reports from buyers and low ratings are reviewed by our team, and license expiry dates are tracked. We may suspend a profile if a check fails or a serious problem is reported.

How long we keep it: uploaded documents are deleted 90 days after a decision. The result of your ID check, your verified name, date of birth and country, your license details, your application and the results of its review are kept while your mentor account exists, and afterwards for as long as the law requires.

When you submit a mentor application, part of the review is automatic. It helps our team decide faster and more consistently. It never rejects anyone: a person on our team makes every rejection, and every decision in a regulated field.

Link checks: our server opens the links you gave as evidence, reads the page title and description, and checks whether the page shows your name or brand. For websites it may also look up, in public domain registration records, how old the website is.

AI-assisted review: we send part of your application to an AI model, Claude, provided by Anthropic, PBC (United States), which scores it and writes a short summary for our team. We send only your title, field, specialty tags, years of experience, story, sample answer, and what the link checks saw (the kind of evidence, the website’s domain, the page title and description). We never send your ID data, date of birth, email address, phone number, bank details, license number or documents, and we remove email addresses, phone numbers and bank account numbers from your text before sending it. Anthropic processes this data for us under its commercial terms and does not use it to train its models.

Account signals: to detect fake or duplicate applications we compare, across accounts, a keyed hash of your network address and of a random identifier stored in your browser, and we look for copied stories, copied sample answers and the same evidence links. The hashes cannot be turned back into an address and are deleted after 180 days.

The decision: automatic approval is possible only when every one of our published rules is met (among them: not a regulated field, ID check passed, names match, all review scores high, at least one piece of evidence checked automatically, and a low risk level), and only if we have switched it on. Everything else is decided by a person, who sees the automatic results. You can ask for any decision to be looked at again by a person, and you can change your application and submit it again.

We use two essential cookies: one keeps you logged in, and one holds a random identifier for your browser that we use only to detect fake or duplicate accounts (it is kept for up to a year). They are not used for advertising or tracking. We also store your language choice in your browser. We do not use advertising or analytics cookies.
To create and secure your account, and to send the emails you need: verification codes, password resets, and notifications about your questions and answers.
To run the marketplace: show mentor profiles, deliver questions and answers, take payments, pay mentors, and issue refunds.
To review mentor applications, partly automatically (see “Automated review of mentor applications”), and to keep the platform safe from fraud and misuse.
To meet legal duties, such as keeping payment records.
We do not sell your personal data.
The mentor you ask receives your name and your question. A seeker receives the mentor’s answer.

Service providers that work for us: our payment bank (card payments and refunds), our identity verification provider (mentors only), Anthropic (the AI-assisted review of mentor applications, mentors only), our email provider (sending emails), and our hosting and database provider. They may only use the data to provide their service to us. When we check a link you gave as evidence, the website it points to receives a request from our server.
Google: if you use Google sign-in, Google learns that you signed in to Wisecall, under Google’s own privacy policy. Nothing about your questions or answers is sent to Google.
Authorities, when the law requires it.
The public can see public profiles, and a mentor’s ratings and reviews (with the reviewer’s name and photo, or “Anonymous asker” when the reviewer’s profile is private).

Our providers may process data outside Georgia, for example in the European Union or the United States (the AI-assisted review of mentor applications is processed in the United States). When that happens, we rely on providers that protect data to a suitable standard.

We keep your account data while your account exists. If you ask us to delete your account, we delete or anonymise your personal data, except records we must keep by law, such as payment records, and data needed to handle a dispute.
Login verification codes and password reset tokens expire within minutes or hours and are stored only as hashes.

You can ask us to give you a copy of your data, correct it, delete it, limit how we use it, or stop using it for something you object to. You can also withdraw a consent you gave. Contact us and we will answer within a reasonable time.
If you believe we handled your data unlawfully, you can complain to the Personal Data Protection Service of Georgia.
Passwords are hashed, connections use HTTPS, and access to data is limited. No system is perfectly secure, so please use a strong, unique password.

Askers must be 16 or older; mentors must be 18 or older and pass the ID check. We ask for a birth year and month when an account is made. If you are under 16 we do not create an account and do not keep what you entered.
If you are 16 or 17, you confirm yourself that your parent or guardian agrees. We do not ask for or keep a parent’s name or email.

What we keep about someone aged 16 or 17, on top of the account data above: their birth year and month (never the day), that they are 16–17, when they confirmed their age and their parent’s or guardian’s agreement, and, for a paid question, when they confirmed that an adult pays. We also keep how many times contact details were stopped in what they wrote, never the words. Their profile can be opened only by them and by our team. Mentors see only their first name and their question, and their questions are never published. We keep this while the account exists, and delete or anonymise it when the account is closed, as in section 9. When someone turns 18 they are treated as an adult from then on.

A parent or guardian can ask us to close the account of someone aged 16 or 17 and delete their data, by email to our support address. If you think someone under 16 has given us data, contact us the same way and we will delete it.
We may update this policy. When we make a meaningful change, we will tell you by email or on the site.

legal.about.title: About Wisecall
legal.about.intro: Wisecall lets people who are just starting out ask a real question and get a real answer from someone who has already done what they want to do.

p: Most of us learned the important things about a career from one honest conversation with the right person. Not everyone has that person in their life. A student who wants to become a doctor, a first-time founder, or a new teacher often has nobody to ask.
Wisecall puts experienced people within reach and makes it worth their time. You pay a fair price, they answer properly, and both sides know what to expect.
1. Find a mentor in your field and read their profile and reviews.
2. Ask your question and pay. The money is held safely until you get your answer.
3. The mentor answers. You get it by email and in your dashboard, and you can leave a review.
If a mentor does not answer within 7 days, you are refunded automatically.

Nobody appears on Wisecall just by signing up. Every mentor confirms their email and passes a government ID and live selfie check with our identity partner: they must be 18 or older, and the name has to match their profile. Then they tell us about their experience, write a sample answer, and show at least one piece of evidence of their work: a portfolio, a website, a company, a diploma, publications or a product. Self-taught experts and business owners are welcome; nobody needs an employer.

Part of the review is automatic: we open the links a mentor gives, and an AI model reads the application to help our team. In regulated fields such as medicine, law and finance we go further: we check the professional license against the official register, and a person always makes the decision. Our team may also ask for one more document.

A person on our team makes every rejection and writes down why. Your ID photos never reach Wisecall, and a mentor’s license number, evidence and documents are never public. Profiles show only badges for the checks passed, with the date.

After approval we keep checking: a new mentor’s first answers are reviewed before you see them, buyers can report a mentor, low ratings are looked at again, and we can suspend a profile at once. We remove people who mislead others.
Mentors set their own price and answer in their own time. Some mentors answer for free. Wisecall keeps a small platform fee to run the service and pays the rest out to the mentor.
Answers are personal experience and opinion, not professional medical, legal, or financial advice. See our Terms for details.
Wisecall is made for Georgia first, in Georgian and English. Questions, answers, and the whole site work in both languages.
Questions or ideas? We would love to hear them. Use the contact page.

mock.a.label: An answer
mock.examples.1.q: I'm a marketing manager who wants to move into product design. Should I start with a course, or build projects first?
mock.examples.1.a: Build first. Pick one real problem, design a small fix for it, and write down your thinking. Two solid case studies beat any certificate. A course helps once you know which gaps you have.
mock.examples.2.q: I want to do a master's in Germany but my IELTS is 6.0. Should I retake it or apply anyway?
mock.examples.2.a: Check each program's minimum first: many accept 6.0 or 6.5, and some technical programs take English B2 without IELTS. If your dream program needs 6.5, retake it; one focused month on writing usually adds half a band.
mock.examples.3.q: I got my first offer as a junior developer in Tbilisi. Is 1,800 ₾ fair, and can I ask for more?
mock.examples.3.a: For a junior role that is the lower-middle range. Ask politely for 10–15% more and give one reason, like a project you built. The worst answer is 'no', and offers are almost never withdrawn for asking once.
mock.examples.4.q: I'm a 5th-year medical student. How do I choose between cardiology and family medicine?
mock.examples.4.a: Spend one week in each before deciding: the daily rhythm matters more than the subject. Cardiology means long training and night shifts; family medicine means more continuity with patients and a calmer schedule.
mock.examples.5.q: I want to open a small coffee stand. What should I test before spending my savings?
mock.examples.5.a: Count people walking past your spot at the hours you'd open, on three different days. Then sell coffee from a table for one weekend before you sign a lease. Real sales will tell you more than any plan.
mock.examples.6.q: I'm a freelance designer. How do I price a logo for a small local business?
mock.examples.6.a: Price the result, not your hours: offer a basic package and a fuller one with a mini brand guide. Most small clients pick the middle option, so always offer three.

ex.label: Example
ex.1.q: I'm self-taught and want my first developer job. Should I learn Python or JavaScript first?
ex.1.a: Pick the one that matches the jobs you can actually apply to. Look at ten local job posts, count which language shows up most, and start there. Depth in one language beats a little of both.
ex.2.q: I'm launching a small product and have no competitors to compare prices with. How do I price it?
ex.2.a: Start from the value, not the cost. Ask five likely customers what they pay today to solve the problem, and price at a fraction of that. You can raise a price later, but it is hard to lower one.
ex.3.q: My class of 25 teenagers talks over me. How do I get their attention without shouting?
ex.3.a: Choose one signal and use it every time: a raised hand, a countdown, or silence at the front. Practise it on the first day, thank the first students who follow it, and wait. Consistency matters more than volume.

faq.4.a: Yes. You pay on your Georgian bank's secure page, in lari. Wisecall never sees or stores your card number.

faq.9.q: How do I become a mentor and get paid?

faq.11.q: Can I ask a follow-up question?
faq.11.a: Yes, one, for free. Once you can read the answer you have 7 days to ask one follow-up question in your Inbox, and the mentor can reply once.
faq.13.q: Can I download or delete my data?
faq.13.a: Yes. In Settings → Account you can download everything we keep about your account, or delete the account. Deleting closes it at once; after 14 days your details are removed, and only payment records stay, without your name, because the law requires them.
faq.14.q: How do I keep my account safe?
faq.14.a: Use a strong password you don't use anywhere else (we refuse passwords known from data breaches) and turn on two-step verification in Settings → Account. There you can also see where you're signed in and sign out other devices.
faq.15.q: What if I'm in an emergency?
faq.15.a: Wisecall is not an emergency service. If you or someone else is in danger, call 112. If a question sounds like an emergency, we don't take the payment and show you where to get help right away.
faq.16.q: Can a mentor hide a bad review?
faq.16.a: No. Only people who paid for and received an answer can leave a review, and mentors can't edit or hide them.
